_description: Sanitized fixtures for ADMISSIBLE_NARROW_FIX_CURSOR_ONESHOT_STREAM_JSON_ASK_AND_OPERATION_LIMIT PART 5. Scenario 1 reconstructs the three real one-byte text-mode empty-success controller invocations (stdout length 1, empty_success). Scenario 2 reconstructs the real stream-json probe: valid NDJSON, a createPlanToolCall + create_plan_request_query interaction workflow, terminal success containing only progress text, zero structured operations. Scenarios 3-4 are constructed Ask-mode-style transcripts exercising the operation-budget boundary. Internal field names (createPlanToolCall, _toolName, create_plan_request_query) match the real installed Cursor CLI's bundled schema (admissible/agent_backend.py comments, RUN_046 forensic audit).

text_mode_empty_success_samples.description: Three real controller invocations under the legacy --output-format text --mode plan preset: exit code 0, stdout length 1, empty stderr. Never valid NDJSON -- caught by the pre-NDJSON whitespace-only stdout check, same as any other empty stdout.

stream_json_probe_createplan_progress_on.description: Live stream-json --mode plan probe: valid NDJSON, model reads the instruction + Mission Contract, emits progress-only assistant messages, calls Cursor's internal createPlan tool, completes a createPlanRequestQuery, and returns terminal success containing only progress text -- no ADMISSIBLE_STRUCTURED_OPERATION block. Must not be treated as a usable proposal.

five_operations_exceeds_effective_maximu.description: A terminal response containing five complete structured operations when the effective per-response maximum (min(system=8, explicit_user=4)) is four. The transport layer parses this as an ordinary successful terminal result; the operation-budget check at admission (validate_coherent_batch_limits / ingest_agent_response) must independently reject it even though nothing in the prompt was violated at the transport level.
